svg.text: Calling introgressions with k-mers (no read mapping)
one 100-kb window of the B73 genome · one sequenced sample = a pool of 6 BC2S3 plants from one plot
Cut the B73 reference genome (RefGen v5) into every 31-letter word (k-mer). Keep only words that occur ONCE.
single-copy k-mer: kept (680 M of 817 M)
repeat k-mer: dropped (present in every genome)
Look the k-mers up in each sample's reads (step 17)
Count all k-mers in the sample's raw reads (KMC). Reads are never mapped, so donor reads are not lost.
k-mers that overlap a donor SNP or indel are missing
r = B73 single-copy k-mers seen in the pool ÷ what a B73 pool of the same depth sees (fit of the B73 controls)
A B73 pool at this depth finds 13,000.
DONOR: the Zd genome has only 27% of
these k-mers, so the pool finds ~3,500:
SEG: shared k-mers (27%) are found as usual;
the rest come only from the B73 half,
Windows → B73 / SEG / DONOR. Switches follow the NAM genetic map; switch rate ρ fitted by maximum likelihood.
